event.summary: No surviving callers of the removed private tmux builder
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2

## TLDR
Considered whether deleting this builder leaves a release or test command pointing at a missing script. No such caller was found at the reviewed revision.

## Details
The entire scripts/build-private-tmux.sh (parent lines 1–167) is deleted. A pinned-revision git grep for build-private-tmux, build-pinned-tmux and TMUX_VERSION across the active tree (excluding forbidden coverage files, plans and historical lore) returned no matches. Commit stat also shows scripts/build-pinned-tmux-ci.sh and .github/release/source-pins.env deleted in the same commit. This rules out direct surviving references, though indirect payload/runtime dependencies remain to be checked during the rest of the assigned pass. SPEC_impl.md:2786–2790 says: "Nothing in an installation requires, looks for or installs a tmux: not the installer, the desktop app, `farhelm helm setup`, or provisioning of a Linux host or a Mac. The running supervisor runs no tmux at all".

Suggested bucket: other (hypothetical maintainer build break only; no established break). Confidence: confirmed absence of searched direct references, source analysis only. proposed_drop: no direct surviving caller; source refutation above. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not consulted. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route for this candidate. No execution or reproduction performed. Continue checking indirect dependencies before concluding the scope.

event.summary: Private tmux builder deletion has no surviving build or payload consumer
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2

## TLDR
Considered whether removing the private tmux builder breaks testing, installation or release payload production. Source analysis found no surviving dependency on the deleted builder; no defect is proposed.

## Details
Assigned patch 01414-000.patch lines 1–173 deletes scripts/build-private-tmux.sh in full (parent lines 1–167). At the parent revision its only executable direct caller is scripts/build-pinned-tmux-ci.sh:75, which is deleted in the same commit. At the reviewed revision, git grep across active sources for build-private-tmux, build-pinned-tmux and TMUX_VERSION returns no matches; another search for .ci-tmux, FARHELM_TEST_TMUX and the deleted tmux/libevent/ncurses checksum variable names finds only .gitignore's obsolete cache exclusion and historical flake evidence, no operational dependency. The replacement test lookup in crates/farhelm-teststate/src/tmux.rs:218–239 resolves the machine's tmux through PATH and prints an explicit SKIPPED message if unavailable. The x86_64 Linux release runtime gate installs the distribution package in .github/dist-build-setup.yml:157–166, with the matching generated step at .github/workflows/release.yml:170–172. This inspection covers the dependency interface only, not an independent review of all replacement test machinery.

The production contract does not require this binary: SPEC.md:5274–5275 states "No supported environment needs tmux: Farhelm neither requires nor looks for one on any machine. A tmux the user runs in a session is one of their own programs, like any other they run there." SPEC_impl.md:2786–2790 states "Nothing in an installation requires, looks for or installs a tmux: not the installer, the desktop app, `farhelm helm setup`, or provisioning of a Linux host or a Mac. The running supervisor runs no tmux at all". Source corroborates the payload side: crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/assets.rs:39–64 lists only the three Farhelm archives and the Mac desktop archive; scripts/install.sh's payload table and dist-workspace.toml have no tmux build/payload reference. SPEC_impl.md:8072–8080 describes the same four payloads and explicitly distinguishes older releases' tmux payloads. The deleted builder's checksum, library and terminfo behavior therefore has no replacement production contract to preserve. SPEC_impl.md:2705–2708 also explicitly removes live tmux as the emulator's test oracle.

Suggested bucket: other (the original hypothetical consequence was a maintainer test/build failure; no established failure). Confidence: confirmed source refutation for the deletion's dependency routes, not observed execution. proposed_drop: no surviving caller or payload consumer, with source and exact contract text above. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage metadata and queue coverage sources were not consulted. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this deletion; no potentially highest finding is being dropped solely on specification acceptance. Caveats: no builds, runtime tests or reproductions were run, and sibling groups own the independent correctness review of changed gate/test implementations. No unresolved premise remains for this candidate.

event.summary: Commit-boundary synthesis still refutes a surviving builder dependency
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2

## TLDR
Revisited whether deleting the private tmux builder breaks a release, test or install command. The parent-to-commit changes remove its consumers together and provide machine tmux for compatibility tests. No defect is proposed; this remains a proposed drop for the caller's decision, not an accepted drop.

## Details
This group has one assigned revision, d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2; analysis compares that revision with its immediate parent rather than relying on the review range's endpoint. Original hypothetical consequence remains a maintainer build/test failure caused by a missing builder or binary. Earlier c1 events establish the only direct executable caller at the parent, scripts/build-pinned-tmux-ci.sh:75, deleted in the same commit, and no surviving source-pin/builder reference. This turn checked the indirect consumers too. In the same commit .github/dist-build-setup.yml replaces building the pinned tmux with apt-get installing tmux for Linux X64 (current lines 157–166), removes .ci-tmux PATH prefixes and --tmux required from runtime commands, and the generated release workflow has the matching install at lines 170–172. scripts/record-test-run.py removes both the source-pins reader and the .ci-tmux binary/hash comparison together with their invocation and --tmux option; scripts/plan-test-hunts.py removes the obsolete source-pin input. The sandbox packers stop archiving .ci-tmux in scripts/tensorlake/rust-tests.ts and sandbox-tests.ts; bootstrap.sh installs tmux and queries the machine binary, and run-rust-shard.sh/run-shard.sh remove the pinned PATH prefixes and obsolete recorder flag. Desktop smoke removes its tmux preflight, old tmux liveness branch and tmux teardown calls; its retained terminal-host checks do not consume the builder output. The CentOS helper removes the retired recorder flag, with no new private-builder consumer.

Production and compatibility-test dependencies are distinct: crates/farhelm-teststate/src/tmux.rs:218–239 intentionally resolves the machine tmux, old_terminals.rs adds explicit skips before its manually constructed old-layout fixtures, and harness/tmux_guard.rs adds the same missing-substrate check. This does not establish production needs tmux. The production asset inventory, directory/download payload consumers, install.sh and sign-sums.yml have no diff across this commit (git diff --exit-code on those exact paths exited successfully with no output); parent-revision searches of those payload/build paths found no tmux payload or checksum consumer. The removed TMUX_SHA256/LIBEVENT_SHA256/NCURSES_SHA256 values only fed the retired test builder, not a signed release asset still expected by installation. Source contract remains SPEC.md:5274–5275: "No supported environment needs tmux: Farhelm neither requires nor looks for one on any machine. A tmux the user runs in a session is one of their own programs, like any other they run there." SPEC_impl.md:2786–2790 says "Nothing in an installation requires, looks for or installs a tmux: not the installer, the desktop app, `farhelm helm setup`, or provisioning of a Linux host or a Mac. The running supervisor runs no tmux at all". The remaining historical-installer warning was separately investigated and source-refuted under l1; it supplies no counterexample.

Suggested bucket: other for the original hypothetical maintainer test/build break; no break established. Confidence: confirmed source-level dependency refutation at the assigned commit boundary, not execution. proposed_drop: no surviving direct or indirect caller/payload/checksum consumer established, with the specific coordinated removals and replacements above. possible_cover: none; no queue/flake/TODO/plan/triage coverage metadata read in this turn. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; no potentially highest issue is dropped solely on specification acceptance. Caveats: this does not independently certify all sibling groups' replacement machinery, and no runtime tests, builds or reproductions were run. No unresolved premise remains for c1.

A separate discovery pass found no additional test-oracle, documentation or build dependency on the deleted private tmux builder. The original hypothetical consequence remains a test/release/install command failing because its builder or payload disappeared; no such route is established.

## Details
Reused all five previous local events and read the complete supplied interface packet before searching. Its runtime-retirement, installer-assurance and grid-compatibility records provide no builder dependency premise and do not refute separate test obligations. New source checks: git log across the complete pinned range, 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a exclusive through 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db inclusive, finds this path changed in cb762a313abbe6da03ae0bf041f07486c4ed4df9 and then deleted in the assigned d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2. This rules out an intervening change in this path's remaining contract, without treating unrelated earlier changes as outside the whole review range. Current searches for pinned/private tmux build references, build-tmux, LIBEVENT_VERSION and NCURSES_VERSION found no remaining build invocation or pin consumer. The prior event preserves the full immediate-parent gate, recorder and sandbox references; l1 separately preserves and refutes the historical-installer gate hypothesis.

Reviewed commit: d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2

## TLDR
A historical installer fixture still requires tmux 3.7c. Check whether a test executes that requirement and implicitly relied on the deleted pinned builder, which could break the release test gate when it now installs the distribution's tmux.

## Details
Pinned-revision search found scripts/fixtures/install-v0.27.0.sh:1401–1456 parsing the machine's tmux version and printing a 3.7c floor refusal. The deleted test builder previously selected tmux 3.7c. Source checks already made: both release gate variants now install/use machine tmux; real old-terminal compatibility fixtures now explicitly select machine tmux; no current source-pins or .ci-tmux operational references survived the deletion. Exact missing premise: whether an active historical-installer test invokes this fixture's real tmux startup path rather than extracting its text or exercising another branch. Next available check: inspect fixture callers and their command/environment inputs at the reviewed commit. Confidence: unverified, investigation in progress, not a substantiated defect. Suggested bucket: other for the suspected maintainer gate failure; no established security or user loss-of-work route. Could-be-highest: no. proposed_drop: false while caller check remains. possible_cover: none. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Historical installer fixture does not require the removed tmux build to succeed
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2

## TLDR
The suspected historical-installer test failure is refuted. The fixture's old tmux floor only controls printed launch advice after installation; it does not refuse installation or need the deleted builder.

## Details
Original suspected consequence: the release test gate could fail because the machine's tmux is older than 3.7c after the pinned builder is deleted. Checked the only active fixture caller, scripts/test-install-sh.sh:2689–2842, and the historical fixture's complete final report block at scripts/fixtures/install-v0.27.0.sh:1396–1468. The caller copies the historical installer into fake releases and tests installation handoff using Mac stand-in tools. It checks successful exit and installation/version/record state, not a successful real Farhelm launch. In the fixture, parsing the real tmux version changes meets_floor and the printed recommendation; lines 1455–1468 contain only printf and shell branches and no failure exit. The installation already happened before this report block, and the function ends after printing. Thus the warning text found by grep was not a startup refusal in the exercised path. No missing runtime prerequisite remains for this lead.

Suggested bucket: other for the original hypothetical maintainer gate failure; no failure established. Confidence: confirmed by caller and source control-flow analysis, not observed execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; a too-old or absent tmux produces advice rather than failing the tested installation handoff. possible_cover: none; queue and coverage metadata not consulted. Could-be-highest: no established security or user loss-of-work route. This revision closes lead l1 as a candidate; it preserves the original suspected consequence rather than silently narrowing it. No build, runtime test or reproduction was run.
